item.title: These are the most common names in Denmark, generation by generation. The most popular name for men today is an international one
item.description: Forget about Jens, Jørgen, and Kirsten: they are all over the names of the streets, but now, they are not used anymore. The most popular name for male kids is not a Danish one, while names for females are more traditional

item.title: European Commission will take part to Trump peace board meeting on Gaza as observer
item.description: EU Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica will attend the meeting in Washington, D.C., the European Commission said. She will join the part of the meeting that focuses on Gaza

item.title: Cold weather continues in Denmark with snow and frost this week
item.description: This week, Denmark will continue to experience cold weather with occasional snow through Friday, according to the meteorologist’s forecast of DMI. High pressure is expected Thursday and Friday, bringing dry weather and periods of sun, but the weekend will see a front moving in from the west with snow turning to rain and milder temperatures. item.title: Danes want Great Prayer Day back, but will not let it decide their vote
item.description: More than half of Danes want Great Prayer Day reinstated as a public holiday, but most say it would not influence their vote in the next election, according to a new poll. item.title: Staff shortages affect well-being and work quality, survey finds
item.description: A shortage of workers is affecting both well-being and the quality of work in Danish workplaces, according to a new survey conducted by Norstat for Lederne. item.title: Greenlanders value the Royal Family – but younger generations are less convinced
item.description: Half of Greenlanders say the Royal Family has personal importance to them, according to a new poll conducted for The Copenhagen Post – but support declines sharply among younger people.

item.title: 200+ Greenland civil servants get same terms as Denmark
item.description: The Danish government has reached an agreement to ensure approximately 230 state civil servants in Greenland receive the same employment terms as those in Denmark. Starting April 1, 2026, these employees, including police and prison officers, will benefit from higher pay, reduced working hours, and improved maternity leave and senior schemes. item.title: Unclear if TV stations will host PM candidate debates
item.description: Broadcasters DR and TV 2 have not yet confirmed if traditional prime ministerial TV duels will occur before the 2026 Danish general election, citing political unpredictability. item.title: New version of physical Rejsekort ready for adults
item.description: Starting Monday, travelers can use “Basiskort,” a new physical alternative to the Rejsekort app. Aimed at seniors, those seeking anonymity, and children without smartphones, the card is currently available for adults, pensioners, and people with disabilities.
